indicators.meaning: Normal Fuse-off Call involves restoring power supply by replacing Horn Gap (HG) or Low Tension (LT) fuses at the distribution transformer or at the consumer's premises .
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must restore power supply following normal fuse-off calls within 4 hours on all working days and within 5 hours on all non-working days in urban areas .
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of cases to be resolved within specified time/standard.
indicators.reported_meaning: % of cases resolved within specified time/standard

indicators.meaning: Normal Fuse-off Call involves restoring power supply by replacing Horn Gap (HG) or Low Tension (LT) fuses at the distribution transformer or at the consumer's premises .
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must restore power supply following normal fuse-off calls within 24 hours in rural areas .
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of cases to be resolved within specified time/standard.
indicators.reported_meaning: % of cases resolved within specified time/standard

indicators.meaning: Line Breakdown refers to restoring electricity supply after overhead line faults or line breakdowns, excluding cases where poles are broken or uprooted .
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must restore power supply following line breakdowns within 12 daylight-hours in urban areas .
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of cases to be resolved within specified time/standard.
indicators.reported_meaning: % of cases resolved within specified time/standard

indicators.meaning: Line Breakdown refers to restoring electricity supply after overhead line faults or line breakdowns, excluding cases where poles are broken or uprooted .
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must restore power supply following line breakdowns within 3 days in rural areas .
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of cases to be resolved within specified time/standard.
indicators.reported_meaning: % of cases resolved within specified time/standard

indicators.meaning: Meter Complaint refers to consumer complaints regarding the inspection, checking of correctness, or replacement of slow, creeping, stuck-up, or burnt meters .
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must inspect and check meter correctness within 7 days .  Defective (slow, creeping, stuck-up) or burnt meters must be replaced within 24 hours in urban areas .
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of cases to be resolved within specified time/standard.
indicators.reported_meaning: % of cases resolved within specified time/standard

indicators.meaning: Meter Complaint refers to consumer complaints regarding the inspection, checking of correctness, or replacement of slow, creeping, stuck-up, or burnt meters .

indicators.type: Application for New Connection or Additional Load
indicators.indicator: Application for new connection/ additional load / reduction of load (Urban)
indicators.meaning: This refers to processing applications and releasing new LT, HT, or EHT electricity connections, or executing contract demand enhancement or reduction .
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must process applications and release connections within the timeframes as notified under the Electricity Supply Code as applicable .
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of cases to be resolved within specified time/standard.
indicators.reported_meaning: % of cases resolved within specified time/standard

indicators.type: Transfer of Ownership and Conversion of service
indicators.indicator: Transfer of ownership and conversion of service
indicators.meaning: This refers to consumer title transfers, consumer category changes, or service phase conversions (LT single-phase to LT three-phase and vice-versa, or LT to HT and vice-versa) .
indicators.standard_specified: Within 15 days after completion of formalities.  If line extension is required, it must be completed within 15 days from the payment of charges and submission of report and within 90 days .  Time taken for change in consumer details must be within 10 days from the date of application .
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of cases to be resolved within specified time/standard.
indicators.reported_meaning: % of cases resolved within specified time/standard

indicators.meaning: This refers to restoring the electricity supply of a consumer whose connection was cut off for non-payment of bills, following receipt of payment .
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must reconnect the consumer's supply within 4 hours of receipt of due payment from the consumer in towns and cities .
indicators.benchmark_meaning: N/A
indicators.reported_meaning: % of cases resolved within specified time/standard

indicators.meaning: Period scheduled outage refers to planned, pre-notified power interruptions carried out by the distribution licensee for maintenance work on the network, which must not exceed 4 times a year .

2021-22.regulation: RERC ( Standards of Performance for Distribution Licensees) Regulations, 2021 | State that the RERC (Standards of Performance for Distribution Licensees) Regulations, 2021 came into force on 15 Apr 2021. It applies from 15 Apr 2021 onward; FY 2021-22 therefore starts before the regulation came into force.

indicators.meaning: Restoring supply in case of supply-related problems/faults like blowing of HT/LT fuse/MCB prior to meter or at distribution transformer or loose connections at meter/service line.
indicators.standard_specified: Restore the supply within Class 1 Cities: Within 2 hours;  Urban Areas: Within 4 hours; Rural Areas: Within 8 hours from reporting.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of complaints to redressed in time
indicators.reported_meaning: % of complaints redressal in time

indicators.meaning: Restoring supply after overhead line or overhead cable breakdowns.
indicators.standard_specified: Restore the supply within  Class 1 Cities: Within 4 hours;  Urban Areas: Within 6 hours;  Rural Areas: Within 10 hours from occurrence.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of complaints to redressed in time
indicators.reported_meaning: % of complaints redressal in time

indicators.meaning: Restoring supply in case of its underground cable breakdown.
indicators.standard_specified: Restore the supply within  Class 1 Cities: Within 12 hours; Urban Areas: Within 12 hours; Rural Areas: Within 24 hours from occurrence.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of complaints to redressed in time
indicators.reported_meaning: % of complaints redressal in time

indicators.indicator: Scheduled outage Default in 24 hours notice
indicators.meaning: Giving consumers advance notification of scheduled outages or planned shutdowns.
indicators.standard_specified: Notification of planned shutdowns must be given at least 24 hours in advance (and on the same day in emergent cases).
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of complaints to redressed in time
indicators.reported_meaning: % of complaints redressal in time

indicators.meaning: The allowable duration limit of power supply interruptions in a day due to planned outages.
indicators.standard_specified: Interruption shall not exceed 7 hours in a day, and supply should normally be restored by 6 pm.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of complaints to redressed in time
indicators.reported_meaning: % of complaints redressal in time

indicators.meaning: Verifying the correctness of a meter at site when a consumer reports that the meter is not functioning properly.
indicators.standard_specified: the licensee must verify the correctness of the meter at site and, if required, replace it within 15 days from the consumer's report
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of complaints to redressed in time
indicators.reported_meaning: % of complaints redressal in time

indicators.meaning: Replacing a consumer's meter that is detected or reported as stopped, damaged, or burnt.
indicators.standard_specified: Replace the meter within 24 hours in urban areas and 72 hours in rural areas from its detection or date of intimation by the consumer.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of complaints to redressed in time
indicators.reported_meaning: % of complaints redressal in time

indicators.meaning: Replacing a stopped, damaged, or burnt meter specifically when it causes a complete loss of supply (no current).
indicators.standard_specified: Replace the meter within 24 hours of reporting by the consumer or detection by the licensee (unless tempered, where it is replaced within 24 hours of consumer depositing security).
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of complaints to redressed in time
indicators.reported_meaning: % of complaints redressal in time

indicators.meaning: Inspecting and informing the consumer of the estimated cost of shifting meters or service lines.
indicators.standard_specified: Inspect and inform the estimated cost to the consumer ithin 15 days of receipt of application.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of complaints to redressed in time
indicators.reported_meaning: % of complaints redressal in time

indicators.meaning: Shifting a consumer's meter after payment of the demand note and obtaining necessary clearances.
indicators.standard_specified: Shift the Meter for LT Consumers: Within 7 working days; HT & EHT Consumers: Within 15 working days from payment and clearance receipt.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of complaints to redressed in time
indicators.reported_meaning: % of complaints redressal in time

indicators.meaning: Shifting a consumer's service line after payment of the demand note and obtaining necessary clearances.
indicators.standard_specified: Shift the service line for LT Consumers: Within 15 working days• HT Consumers: Within 1 month from payment and clearance receipt.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of complaints to redressed in time
indicators.reported_meaning: % of complaints redressal in time

indicators.type: Release of New Connections or additional power
indicators.meaning: Releasing new electricity connections or additional power to different categories of consumers.
indicators.standard_specified: Must be released as per the norms specified in the RERC (Supply Code & Connected Matters) Regulations, 2021.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of complaints to redressed in time
indicators.reported_meaning: % of complaints redressal in time

indicators.type: Transfer of ownership or change of category
indicators.indicator: Transfer of ownership or change of category
indicators.meaning: Transferring the ownership of connection or changing the category of supply on the existing system.
indicators.standard_specified: Ownership of the connection or change of category on the existing system shall be transferred within 1 month from receipt of necessary documents certifying the transfer/change.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of complaints to redressed in time
indicators.reported_meaning: % of complaints redressal in time

indicators.meaning: Disconnecting supply upon consumer request and clearance of dues.
indicators.standard_specified: Disconnect the supply in Class 1 Cities: Within 3 working days;  Urban & Rural Areas: Within 7 working days from receipt of request and clearance.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of complaints to redressed in time
indicators.reported_meaning: % of complaints redressal in time

indicators.meaning: Refunding security/money and issuing a "No-Dues Certificate" upon permanent disconnection.
indicators.standard_specified: Shall issue the certificate within 7 days from the date of disconnection or from the date of clearing the admissible dues, whichever is later.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of complaints to redressed in time
indicators.reported_meaning: % of complaints redressal in time

indicators.meaning: Restoring power supply to a disconnected (DC) consumer after they clear their dues.

indicators.standard_specified: Must be released as per the norms specified in the RERC (Supply Code & Connected Matters) Regulations, 2021.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of complaints to redressed in time
indicators.reported_meaning: % of complaints redressal in time

indicators.type: Transfer of ownership or change of category
indicators.indicator: Transfer of ownership or change of category
indicators.meaning: Transferring the ownership of connection or changing the category of supply on the existing system.
indicators.standard_specified: Ownership of the connection or change of category on the existing system shall be transferred within 1 month from receipt of necessary documents certifying the transfer/change.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of complaints to redressed in time
indicators.reported_meaning: % of complaints redressal in time

indicators.meaning: Disconnecting supply upon consumer request and clearance of dues.
indicators.standard_specified: Disconnect the supply in Class 1 Cities: Within 3 working days;  Urban & Rural Areas: Within 7 working days from receipt of request and clearance.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of complaints to redressed in time
indicators.reported_meaning: % of complaints redressal in time

indicators.meaning: Refunding security/money and issuing a "No-Dues Certificate" upon permanent disconnection.
indicators.standard_specified: Shall issue the certificate within 7 days from the date of disconnection or from the date of clearing the admissible dues, whichever is later.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of complaints to redressed in time
indicators.reported_meaning: % of complaints redressal in time

indicators.meaning: Restoring power supply to a disconnected (DC) consumer after they clear their dues.
indicators.standard_specified: Restore the supply within 6 working hours of clearing the dues (if infrastructure erection is required, as per RERC Supply Code Regulations, 2021).
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of complaints to redressed in time
indicators.reported_meaning: % of complaints redressal in time

indicators.meaning: Serving regular electricity bills on the consumers.
indicators.standard_specified: Served as per the timelines given in the RERC (Supply Code & Connected Matters) Regulations, 2021 (and within 7 days of written complaint if the first bill is delayed).
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of complaints to redressed in time
indicators.reported_meaning: % of complaints redressal in time

indicators.meaning: Restoring supply in case of supply-related problems/faults like blowing of HT/LT fuse/MCB prior to meter or at distribution transformer or loose connections at meter/service line.
indicators.standard_specified: Restore the supply within Class 1 Cities: Within 2 hours;  Urban Areas: Within 4 hours; Rural Areas: Within 8 hours from reporting.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of complaints to redressed in time
indicators.reported_meaning: % of complaints redressal in time

indicators.meaning: Restoring supply after overhead line or overhead cable breakdowns.
indicators.standard_specified: Restore the supply within  Class 1 Cities: Within 4 hours;  Urban Areas: Within 6 hours;  Rural Areas: Within 10 hours from occurrence.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of complaints to redressed in time
indicators.reported_meaning: % of complaints redressal in time

indicators.meaning: Restoring supply in case of its underground cable breakdown.
indicators.standard_specified: Restore the supply within  Class 1 Cities: Within 12 hours; Urban Areas: Within 12 hours; Rural Areas: Within 24 hours from occurrence.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of complaints to redressed in time
indicators.reported_meaning: % of complaints redressal in time

indicators.indicator: Scheduled outage Default in 24 hours notice
indicators.meaning: Giving consumers advance notification of scheduled outages or planned shutdowns.
indicators.standard_specified: Notification of planned shutdowns must be given at least 24 hours in advance (and on the same day in emergent cases).
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of complaints to redressed in time
indicators.reported_meaning: % of complaints redressal in time

indicators.meaning: The allowable duration limit of power supply interruptions in a day due to planned outages.
indicators.standard_specified: Interruption shall not exceed 7 hours in a day, and supply should normally be restored by 6 pm.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of complaints to redressed in time
indicators.reported_meaning: % of complaints redressal in time

indicators.meaning: Verifying the correctness of a meter at site when a consumer reports that the meter is not functioning properly.
indicators.standard_specified: the licensee must verify the correctness of the meter at site and, if required, replace it within 15 days from the consumer's report
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of complaints to redressed in time
indicators.reported_meaning: % of complaints redressal in time

indicators.meaning: Replacing a consumer's meter that is detected or reported as stopped, damaged, or burnt.
indicators.standard_specified: Replace the meter within 24 hours in urban areas and 72 hours in rural areas from its detection or date of intimation by the consumer.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of complaints to redressed in time
indicators.reported_meaning: % of complaints redressal in time

indicators.meaning: Replacing a stopped, damaged, or burnt meter specifically when it causes a complete loss of supply (no current).
indicators.standard_specified: Replace the meter within 24 hours of reporting by the consumer or detection by the licensee (unless tempered, where it is replaced within 24 hours of consumer depositing security).
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of complaints to redressed in time
indicators.reported_meaning: % of complaints redressal in time

indicators.meaning: Inspecting and informing the consumer of the estimated cost of shifting meters or service lines.
indicators.standard_specified: Inspect and inform the estimated cost to the consumer ithin 15 days of receipt of application.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of complaints to redressed in time
indicators.reported_meaning: % of complaints redressal in time

indicators.meaning: Shifting a consumer's meter after payment of the demand note and obtaining necessary clearances.
indicators.standard_specified: Shift the Meter for LT Consumers: Within 7 working days; HT & EHT Consumers: Within 15 working days from payment and clearance receipt.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: % of complaints to redressed in time
indicators.reported_meaning: % of complaints redressal in time

indicators.meaning: Shifting a consumer's service line after payment of the demand note and obtaining necessary clearances.

discoms.full_name: North Bihar Power Distribution Company Limited

2021-22.regulation: Bihar Electricity Regulatory Commission (Standards of Performance of Distribution Licensee) Regulations, 2006 | Bihar Electricity Regulatory Commission (Standards of Performance of Distribution Licensee) (First Amendment) Regulations, 2012 | Bihar Electricity Regulatory Commission (Standards of Performance of Distribution Licensee) (First Amendment) Regulations, 2017

indicators.meaning: Replacing blown Horn Gap (HG) or Low Tension (LT) fuses at distribution transformers or consumer premises.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must replace blown fuses and restore power supply within 4 hours in cities and towns.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of calls received must be rectified within the specified time limit.

indicators.meaning: Replacing blown Horn Gap (HG) or Low Tension (LT) fuses at distribution transformers or consumer premises.
indicators.standard_specified: In rural areas, the licensee is mandated to replace blown fuses and restore the supply within 24 hours.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of calls received must be rectified within the specified time limit.

indicators.meaning: Repairing overhead distribution lines or cables, excluding cases with broken or uprooted poles.
indicators.standard_specified: For overhead line or cable failures in cities and towns, the utility must resolve the breakdown and restore electricity within 6 hours.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of cases must be resolved within the specified time limit.

indicators.meaning: Repairing overhead distribution lines or cables, excluding cases with broken or uprooted poles.
indicators.standard_specified: Power supply restoration following an overhead line or cable breakdown in rural areas must be completed within 36 hours.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of cases must be resolved within the specified time limit.

indicators.meaning: Locating, repairing, and re-energising the system following faults in underground cables.
indicators.standard_specified: The licensee is required to locate, repair, and re-energize the network within 24 hours of an underground cable fault in urban areas.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of cases must be resolved within the specified time limit.

indicators.meaning: Locating, repairing, and re-energising the system following faults in underground cables.
indicators.standard_specified: Underground cable faults in rural areas must be located and fully repaired to restore supply within 48 hours.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of cases must be resolved within the specified time limit.

indicators.meaning: Replacing or repairing failed distribution transformers and restoring consumer service lines.
indicators.standard_specified: The utility must replace or repair a failed distribution transformer and restore supply to consumers within 24 hours in urban areas.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of failed transformers must be replaced within the specified time limit.

indicators.meaning: Replacing or repairing failed distribution transformers and restoring consumer service lines.
indicators.standard_specified: Following a distribution transformer failure in rural areas, the company must complete replacement and restore supply within 72 hours.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of failed transformers must be replaced within the specified time limit.

indicators.meaning: Pre-arranged shut-downs of equipment and lines for necessary maintenance work.
indicators.standard_specified: The maximum duration of a pre-planned maintenance outage is strictly capped at 12 hours in a single stretch.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of scheduled outages must comply with the maximum duration standard.

indicators.meaning: Pre-arranged shut-downs of equipment and lines for necessary maintenance work.
indicators.standard_specified: During pre-arranged maintenance, the utility must ensure power supply is fully restored not later than 6:00 PM.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of planned outages must have supply restored by 6:00 PM.

indicators.meaning: Rectification of line faults and replacement of public street lighting fixtures.
indicators.standard_specified: The licensee must rectify line faults or replace fused and defective public street lighting fixtures as soon as possible.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 90% of street light complaints must be resolved.

indicators.meaning: Total allowable rate of billing errors across all prepared accounts.
indicators.standard_specified: The total number of billing mistakes across all processed accounts must be kept under a maximum limit of 1% of total bills prepared.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: The overall error rate across all prepared bills must remain under the 1% cap.

indicators.meaning: Correcting billing errors where no additional on-site inspection or information is required.
indicators.standard_specified: When a billing complaint is raised and no on-site investigation is needed, the revised bill must be issued within 24 working hours.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 99% of complaints must be resolved within the specified time limit.

indicators.meaning: Correcting billing errors where inspection or meter verification is needed for Low Tension (LT) consumers.
indicators.standard_specified: If a billing complaint requires field inspection or meter checking for LT consumers, the licensee must issue the revised bill within 7 working days.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 99% of complaints must be resolved within the specified time limit.

indicators.meaning: Correcting billing errors where inspection or meter verification is needed for High Tension (HT) consumers.
indicators.standard_specified: For HT consumer billing disputes requiring on-site verification, the revised bill must be completed and issued within 15 days.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 99% of complaints must be resolved within the specified time limit.

indicators.meaning: The maximum allowable proportion of active meters that are malfunctioning or defective.
indicators.standard_specified: The utility must manage its network such that the overall proportion of faulty meters in service does not exceed 3% of the total meters.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: The overall percentage of faulty meters in service must be kept below the 3% ceiling.

indicators.meaning: Testing and replacing defective, creeping, or stuck meters in urban areas.
indicators.standard_specified: For defective meters in urban areas, the licensee must inspect them within 7 days and complete the replacement within 15 days thereafter.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 99% of cases in urban areas must be resolved within the specified timelines.

indicators.meaning: Testing and replacing defective, creeping, or stuck meters in rural areas.
indicators.standard_specified: The utility must inspect a reported defective meter in rural areas within 15 days and replace it within 15 days of that inspection.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 98% of cases in rural areas must be resolved within the specified timelines.

indicators.meaning: Replacing burnt meters due to network failures (such as high voltage or loose contacts).
indicators.standard_specified: When a meter burns out due to utility-attributable factors, it must be replaced at licensee cost within 7 days.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 99% of urban and 98% of rural complaints must be resolved within the standard.

indicators.meaning: Replacing burnt meters due to consumer overloading, tampering, or water exposure.
indicators.standard_specified: If a meter is burnt due to consumer-side issues, the licensee must replace it within 14 days of receiving payment or a replacement meter.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 99% of urban and 98% of rural complaints must be resolved within the standard.

indicators.meaning: Limit on the symmetry deviation among phase voltages at the point of supply.
indicators.standard_specified: The phase voltage unbalance at the consumer's point of supply must be maintained so that it does not exceed 3%.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 98% of cases related to voltage unbalance must be resolved.

indicators.meaning: Resolving voltage issues where system network expansion is not required.
indicators.standard_specified: The licensee must resolve complaints regarding voltage levels within 10 days when no network expansion is required.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 98% of voltage fluctuation complaints must be resolved within the specified timeline.

indicators.meaning: Resolving voltage issues where system capacity reinforcement or upgrade is required.
indicators.standard_specified: Where resolving voltage fluctuations requires system up-gradation or network enhancement, the works must be completed within 120 days.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 98% of voltage fluctuation complaints must be resolved within the specified timeline.

indicators.meaning: Resolving voltage issues when a new substation needs to be erected.
indicators.standard_specified: When resolving a voltage issue requires erecting a new substation, the utility must complete it within the time period approved by the Commission.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 98% of voltage fluctuation complaints must be resolved within the specified timeline.

indicators.meaning: Releasing supply where distribution mains are already in place.

indicators.meaning: Replacing blown Horn Gap (HG) or Low Tension (LT) fuses at distribution transformers or consumer premises.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must replace blown fuses and restore power supply within 4 hours in cities and towns.

indicators.meaning: Replacing blown Horn Gap (HG) or Low Tension (LT) fuses at distribution transformers or consumer premises.
indicators.standard_specified: In rural areas, the licensee is mandated to replace blown fuses and restore the supply within 24 hours.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of calls received must be rectified within the specified time limit.

indicators.meaning: Repairing overhead distribution lines or cables, excluding cases with broken or uprooted poles.
indicators.standard_specified: For overhead line or cable failures in cities and towns, the utility must resolve the breakdown and restore electricity within 6 hours.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of cases must be resolved within the specified time limit.

indicators.meaning: Repairing overhead distribution lines or cables, excluding cases with broken or uprooted poles.
indicators.standard_specified: Power supply restoration following an overhead line or cable breakdown in rural areas must be completed within 36 hours.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of cases must be resolved within the specified time limit.

indicators.meaning: Locating, repairing, and re-energising the system following faults in underground cables.
indicators.standard_specified: The licensee is required to locate, repair, and re-energize the network within 24 hours of an underground cable fault in urban areas.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of cases must be resolved within the specified time limit.

indicators.meaning: Locating, repairing, and re-energising the system following faults in underground cables.
indicators.standard_specified: Underground cable faults in rural areas must be located and fully repaired to restore supply within 48 hours.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of cases must be resolved within the specified time limit.

indicators.meaning: Replacing or repairing failed distribution transformers and restoring consumer service lines.
indicators.standard_specified: The utility must replace or repair a failed distribution transformer and restore supply to consumers within 24 hours in urban areas.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of failed transformers must be replaced within the specified time limit.

indicators.meaning: Replacing or repairing failed distribution transformers and restoring consumer service lines.
indicators.standard_specified: Following a distribution transformer failure in rural areas, the company must complete replacement and restore supply within 72 hours.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of failed transformers must be replaced within the specified time limit.

indicators.meaning: Pre-arranged shut-downs of equipment and lines for necessary maintenance work.
indicators.standard_specified: The maximum duration of a pre-planned maintenance outage is strictly capped at 12 hours in a single stretch.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of scheduled outages must comply with the maximum duration standard.

indicators.meaning: Pre-arranged shut-downs of equipment and lines for necessary maintenance work.
indicators.standard_specified: During pre-arranged maintenance, the utility must ensure power supply is fully restored not later than 6:00 PM.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of planned outages must have supply restored by 6:00 PM.

indicators.meaning: Rectification of line faults and replacement of public street lighting fixtures.
indicators.standard_specified: The licensee must rectify line faults or replace fused and defective public street lighting fixtures as soon as possible.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 90% of street light complaints must be resolved.

indicators.meaning: Total allowable rate of billing errors across all prepared accounts.
indicators.standard_specified: The total number of billing mistakes across all processed accounts must be kept under a maximum limit of 1% of total bills prepared.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: The overall error rate across all prepared bills must remain under the 1% cap.

indicators.meaning: Correcting billing errors where no additional on-site inspection or information is required.
indicators.standard_specified: When a billing complaint is raised and no on-site investigation is needed, the revised bill must be issued within 24 working hours.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 99% of complaints must be resolved within the specified time limit.

indicators.meaning: Correcting billing errors where inspection or meter verification is needed for Low Tension (LT) consumers.
indicators.standard_specified: If a billing complaint requires field inspection or meter checking for LT consumers, the licensee must issue the revised bill within 7 working days.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 99% of complaints must be resolved within the specified time limit.

indicators.meaning: Correcting billing errors where inspection or meter verification is needed for High Tension (HT) consumers.
indicators.standard_specified: For HT consumer billing disputes requiring on-site verification, the revised bill must be completed and issued within 15 days.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 99% of complaints must be resolved within the specified time limit.

indicators.meaning: The maximum allowable proportion of active meters that are malfunctioning or defective.
indicators.standard_specified: The utility must manage its network such that the overall proportion of faulty meters in service does not exceed 3% of the total meters.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: The overall percentage of faulty meters in service must be kept below the 3% ceiling.

indicators.meaning: Testing and replacing defective, creeping, or stuck meters in urban areas.
indicators.standard_specified: For defective meters in urban areas, the licensee must inspect them within 7 days and complete the replacement within 15 days thereafter.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 99% of cases in urban areas must be resolved within the specified timelines.

indicators.meaning: Testing and replacing defective, creeping, or stuck meters in rural areas.
indicators.standard_specified: The utility must inspect a reported defective meter in rural areas within 15 days and replace it within 15 days of that inspection.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 98% of cases in rural areas must be resolved within the specified timelines.

indicators.meaning: Replacing burnt meters due to network failures (such as high voltage or loose contacts).
indicators.standard_specified: When a meter burns out due to utility-attributable factors, it must be replaced at licensee cost within 7 days.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 99% of urban and 98% of rural complaints must be resolved within the standard.

indicators.meaning: Replacing burnt meters due to consumer overloading, tampering, or water exposure.
indicators.standard_specified: If a meter is burnt due to consumer-side issues, the licensee must replace it within 14 days of receiving payment or a replacement meter.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 99% of urban and 98% of rural complaints must be resolved within the standard.

indicators.meaning: Limit on the symmetry deviation among phase voltages at the point of supply.
indicators.standard_specified: The phase voltage unbalance at the consumer's point of supply must be maintained so that it does not exceed 3%.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 98% of cases related to voltage unbalance must be resolved.

indicators.meaning: Resolving voltage issues where system network expansion is not required.
indicators.standard_specified: The licensee must resolve complaints regarding voltage levels within 10 days when no network expansion is required.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 98% of voltage fluctuation complaints must be resolved within the specified timeline.

indicators.standard_specified: Where resolving voltage fluctuations requires system up-gradation or network enhancement, the works must be completed within 120 days.

indicators.meaning: Replacing burnt meters due to network failures (such as high voltage or loose contacts).

indicators.meaning: Resolving voltage issues where system network expansion is not required.

indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 98% of voltage fluctuation complaints must be resolved within the specified timeline.

indicators.standard_specified: Where resolving voltage fluctuations requires system up-gradation or network enhancement, the works must be completed within 120 days.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 98% of voltage fluctuation complaints must be resolved within the specified timeline.

indicators.meaning: Resolving voltage issues when a new substation needs to be erected.
indicators.standard_specified: When resolving a voltage issue requires erecting a new substation, the utility must complete it within the time period approved by the Commission.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 98% of voltage fluctuation complaints must be resolved within the specified timeline.

indicators.meaning: Releasing supply where distribution mains are already in place.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must release a new electricity connection within 30 days of receiving a completed application and requisite charges.

indicators.benchmark_meaning: All cases (100%) of release of connection must be completed within the specified limits.

indicators.meaning: Releasing 11 KV supply when network extension is required.

indicators.benchmark_meaning: All cases (100%) of release of connection must be completed within the specified limits.

indicators.meaning: Releasing 33 KV supply when network extension is required.

indicators.benchmark_meaning: All cases (100%) of release of connection must be completed within the specified limits.

indicators.meaning: Releasing EHT supply when network extension is required.

indicators.meaning: Releasing supply when a new substation must be erected.

indicators.meaning: Processing the transfer of ownership of a service connection to a new owner.

indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 98% of cases related to title transfer must be resolved within specified limits.

indicators.meaning: Processing a consumer's request to reduce contract demand.

indicators.meaning: Replacing blown Horn Gap (HG) or Low Tension (LT) fuses at distribution transformers or consumer premises.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must replace blown fuses and restore power supply within 4 hours in cities and towns.

indicators.meaning: Replacing blown Horn Gap (HG) or Low Tension (LT) fuses at distribution transformers or consumer premises.

indicators.standard_specified: For HT consumer billing disputes requiring on-site verification, the revised bill must be completed and issued within 15 days.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 99% of complaints must be resolved within the specified time limit.

indicators.meaning: The maximum allowable proportion of active meters that are malfunctioning or defective.
indicators.standard_specified: The utility must manage its network such that the overall proportion of faulty meters in service does not exceed 3% of the total meters.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: The overall percentage of faulty meters in service must be kept below the 3% ceiling.

indicators.meaning: Testing and replacing defective, creeping, or stuck meters in urban areas.
indicators.standard_specified: For defective meters in urban areas, the licensee must inspect them within 7 days and complete the replacement within 15 days thereafter.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 99% of cases in urban areas must be resolved within the specified timelines.

indicators.meaning: Testing and replacing defective, creeping, or stuck meters in rural areas.
indicators.standard_specified: The utility must inspect a reported defective meter in rural areas within 15 days and replace it within 15 days of that inspection.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 98% of cases in rural areas must be resolved within the specified timelines.

indicators.meaning: Replacing burnt meters due to network failures (such as high voltage or loose contacts).
indicators.standard_specified: When a meter burns out due to utility-attributable factors, it must be replaced at licensee cost within 7 days.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 99% of urban and 98% of rural complaints must be resolved within the standard.

indicators.meaning: Replacing burnt meters due to consumer overloading, tampering, or water exposure.
indicators.standard_specified: If a meter is burnt due to consumer-side issues, the licensee must replace it within 14 days of receiving payment or a replacement meter.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 99% of urban and 98% of rural complaints must be resolved within the standard.

indicators.meaning: Limit on the symmetry deviation among phase voltages at the point of supply.
indicators.standard_specified: The phase voltage unbalance at the consumer's point of supply must be maintained so that it does not exceed 3%.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 98% of cases related to voltage unbalance must be resolved.

indicators.meaning: Resolving voltage issues where system network expansion is not required.
indicators.standard_specified: The licensee must resolve complaints regarding voltage levels within 10 days when no network expansion is required.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 98% of voltage fluctuation complaints must be resolved within the specified timeline.

indicators.meaning: Resolving voltage issues where system capacity reinforcement or upgrade is required.
indicators.standard_specified: Where resolving voltage fluctuations requires system up-gradation or network enhancement, the works must be completed within 120 days.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 98% of voltage fluctuation complaints must be resolved within the specified timeline.

indicators.meaning: Resolving voltage issues when a new substation needs to be erected.
indicators.standard_specified: When resolving a voltage issue requires erecting a new substation, the utility must complete it within the time period approved by the Commission.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 98% of voltage fluctuation complaints must be resolved within the specified timeline.

indicators.meaning: Releasing supply where distribution mains are already in place.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must release a new electricity connection within 30 days of receiving a completed application and requisite charges.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: All cases (100%) of release of connection must be completed within the specified limits.

indicators.meaning: Releasing LT supply when distribution main extension is required.
indicators.standard_specified: Where an LT connection requires expanding or enhancing the distribution network, the supply must be released within 30 days of receiving payment.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: All cases (100%) of release of connection must be completed within the specified limits.

indicators.meaning: Releasing 11 KV supply when network extension is required.
indicators.standard_specified: The licensee must complete the necessary 11 KV network expansion and release supply within 60 days of payment of prescribed charges.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: All cases (100%) of release of connection must be completed within the specified limits.

indicators.meaning: Releasing 33 KV supply when network extension is required.
indicators.standard_specified: For new HT 33 KV connections requiring network extension, the licensee must complete the work and release supply within 90 days of payment.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: All cases (100%) of release of connection must be completed within the specified limits.

indicators.meaning: Releasing EHT supply when network extension is required.
indicators.standard_specified: When releasing an Extra High Tension supply involves network extension, the connection must be completed and energized within 180 days of payment.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: All cases (100%) of release of connection must be completed within the specified limits.

indicators.meaning: Releasing supply when a new substation must be erected.
indicators.standard_specified: If releasing a new connection requires erecting a substation, the licensee must complete the installation within the timeframe approved by the Commission.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: All cases (100%) of release of connection must be completed within the specified limits.

indicators.meaning: Processing the transfer of ownership of a service connection to a new owner.
indicators.standard_specified: The licensee must process and finalize the transfer of connection ownership within 7 days of receiving the documents and prescribed fee.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 98% of cases related to title transfer must be resolved within specified limits.

indicators.meaning: Processing the change of consumer/tariff category.
indicators.standard_specified: A request for tariff or category conversion must be processed and completed by the licensee within 7 days of receiving the required documents.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 98% of cases related to conversion must be resolved within specified limits.

indicators.meaning: Processing a consumer's request to reduce contract demand.
indicators.standard_specified: The licensee must complete the load reduction process within the notice period specified in the Electricity Supply Code.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 98% of load reduction requests must be completed within the notice period.

indicators.meaning: Replacing blown fuses at distribution transformers or consumer premises.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must replace blown fuses and restore power supply within 2 hours of receiving a complaint in Class-I Cities.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of total fuse-off calls must be rectified within the specified time limits.

indicators.meaning: Replacing blown fuses at distribution transformers or consumer premises.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must replace blown fuses and restore power supply within 4 hours of receiving a complaint in Urban Areas.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of total fuse-off calls must be rectified within the specified time limits.

indicators.meaning: Replacing blown fuses at distribution transformers or consumer premises.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must replace blown fuses and restore power supply within 6 hours of receiving a complaint in Rural Areas.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of total fuse-off calls must be rectified within the specified time limits.

indicators.meaning: Repairing overhead distribution lines or cables, excluding cases with broken or uprooted poles.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must resolve overhead line or cable breakdowns and restore supply within 2 hours of occurrence in Class-I Cities.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of overall cases of line breakdowns must have power restored within specified limits.

indicators.meaning: Repairing overhead distribution lines or cables, excluding cases with broken or uprooted poles.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must resolve overhead line or cable breakdowns and restore supply within 3 hours of occurrence in Urban Areas.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of overall cases of line breakdowns must have power restored within specified limits.

indicators.meaning: Repairing overhead distribution lines or cables, excluding cases with broken or uprooted poles.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must resolve overhead line or cable breakdowns and restore supply within 24 hours of occurrence in Rural Areas.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of overall cases of line breakdowns must have power restored within specified limits.

indicators.indicator: Underground Cable Breakdowns (Class-I Cities & Urban Areas)
indicators.meaning: Locating, repairing, and re-energising the system following underground cable network faults.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must locate, repair, and restore power supply within 12 hours of an underground cable breakdown in Class-I Cities and Urban Areas.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of overall cases of line breakdowns must have power restored within specified limits.

indicators.meaning: Locating, repairing, and re-energising the system following underground cable network faults.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must locate, repair, and restore power supply within 48 hours of an underground cable breakdown in Rural Areas.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of overall cases of line breakdowns must have power restored within specified limits.

indicators.meaning: Replacing or repairing failed distribution transformers and restoring consumer service lines.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must replace or repair a failed distribution transformer and restore supply within 6 hours of receiving a complaint in Class-I Cities.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of total failed distribution transformers must be replaced within the specified time limits.

indicators.meaning: Replacing or repairing failed distribution transformers and restoring consumer service lines.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must replace or repair a failed distribution transformer and restore supply within 8 hours of receiving a complaint in Urban Areas.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of total failed distribution transformers must be replaced within the specified time limits.

indicators.meaning: Replacing or repairing failed distribution transformers and restoring consumer service lines.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must replace or repair a failed distribution transformer and restore supply within 48 hours of receiving a complaint in Rural Areas.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of total failed distribution transformers must be replaced within the specified time limits.

indicators.meaning: Restoring supply after disconnection due to non-payment, upon settlement of dues.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must restore power supply to a consumer disconnected for non-payment within 2 hours of prepaid meter recharge.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of reconnection of supply cases must be completed within the specified limits.

indicators.meaning: Advance notification of pre-planned outages for system maintenance.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must notify consumers of any scheduled outages (excluding load-shedding) at least 24 hours in advance.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of scheduled outages must comply with the advance notification standard.

indicators.meaning: Restricting duration of pre-planned maintenance shutdowns on 11kV feeders.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must limit the total duration of scheduled outages to not exceed 12 hours in a month for any 11kV feeder in Class-I and Urban areas.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of scheduled outages must comply with the monthly duration limits.

indicators.meaning: Restricting duration of pre-planned maintenance shutdowns on 11kV feeders.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must limit the total duration of scheduled outages to not exceed 24 hours in a month for any 11kV feeder in Rural Areas.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of scheduled outages must comply with the monthly duration limits.

indicators.indicator: Shifting of Meters/Service Lines (Cost Estimation - Class-I)
indicators.meaning: Inspecting and informing the consumer of estimated shifting costs.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must inspect and inform the estimated cost to the consumer within 7 days of receiving the shifting application in Class-I Cities.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of shifting requests must comply with the inspection and estimation timeline.

indicators.indicator: Shifting of Meters/Service Lines (Cost Estimation - Urban)
indicators.meaning: Inspecting and informing the consumer of estimated shifting costs.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must inspect and inform the estimated cost to the consumer within 10 days of receiving the shifting application in Urban Areas.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of shifting requests must comply with the inspection and estimation timeline.

indicators.indicator: Shifting of Meters/Service Lines (Cost Estimation - Rural)
indicators.meaning: Inspecting and informing the consumer of estimated shifting costs.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must inspect and inform the estimated cost to the consumer within 15 days of receiving the shifting application in Rural Areas.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of shifting requests must comply with the inspection and estimation timeline.

indicators.meaning: Physically shifting the meter or service line after payments and clearances.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must complete the physical shifting of the meter or service line within 7 days from the date of payment and clearances.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of shifting requests must be fully executed within the specified work schedule.

indicators.meaning: Processing applications and releasing supply under the Electricity Supply Code.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must release new connections, enhance load, or reduce contracted load as per the provisions of the UPERC Electricity Supply Code.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of connection and load change cases must be processed within the Supply Code limits.

indicators.meaning: Transferring the electricity account title to a new owner.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must execute and complete the transfer of ownership of a service connection within the second billing cycle from receipt of application.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of ownership transfer cases must be resolved within the specified billing cycles.

indicators.meaning: Changing consumer or tariff categories (e.g., converting phases or voltage levels).
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must convert the service connection phase or voltage level within the second billing cycle from payment of necessary charges.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of category change cases must be resolved within the specified billing cycles.

indicators.meaning: Providing electricity supply for temporary periods.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must provide temporary supply of power as per Section 4.10 of the UPERC Electricity Supply Code.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of temporary supply cases must be provided within the specified timelines.

indicators.meaning: Processing requests for permanent service disconnection.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must execute requests for permanent disconnection as per Section 4.38 of the UPERC Electricity Supply Code.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of permanent disconnection requests must be processed within the Supply Code limits.

indicators.meaning: Maintaining overall meter health across the distribution system.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must maintain the percentage of defective meters in service at a value not greater than 3% of the total meters in service.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: The overall percentage of faulty or defective active meters across the network must not exceed the 3% cap.

indicators.meaning: Managing the error rate of issued bills requiring modifications.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must limit the percentage of bills requiring modifications following complaints to not exceed 0.1% of the total bills issued.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: The overall billing error rate requiring corrections must remain under the 0.1% ceiling.

indicators.meaning: Advance announcement of power cuts or load shedding schedules.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must submit its load shedding plan to the Commission for approval and publish it in the newspaper at least 48 hours in advance.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: The licensee must fully comply with the advance approval and 48-hour newspaper publication standard.

indicators.meaning: Meeting target duration of electricity supply to consumers.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must achieve the standard of performance in at least 96% against the scheduled hours of power supply.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 96% of the scheduled hours of power supply must be successfully met and maintained.

indicators.meaning: Restoring power supply after a High Tension (HT) grid or line failure in Corporation limits.

indicators.meaning: Restoring power supply after a High Tension (HT) grid or line failure in mountainous or hilly terrain.

indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 75% of cases must be resolved within the standard; 20% of the remaining cases must be resolved within 24 hours of the complaint.

indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 75% of cases must be resolved within the standard; 20% of the remaining cases must be resolved within 24 hours of the complaint.

indicators.indicator: Fault in Transformer Structure, LT Line, or Pillar Box (Rural Areas)
indicators.meaning: Restoring supply after Low Tension line faults, distribution pillar box defects, or structural faults.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must resolve the fault in the transformer structure, LT line, or pillar box and restore power within 6 hours in Rural Areas.

indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must resolve the fault in the transformer structure, LT line, or pillar box and restore power within 12 hours in Hill Areas.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 75% of cases must be resolved within the standard; 20% of the remaining cases must be resolved within 24 hours of the complaint.

indicators.meaning: Replacing or repairing failed distribution transformers on the urban network.

indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of failed distribution transformers must be replaced within the specified time limit.

indicators.meaning: Replacing or repairing failed distribution transformers on the municipal, rural, or hill network.
indicators.standard_specified: The distribution licensee must replace or repair a failed distribution transformer and restore supply within 48 hours in Municipalities, Rural, or Hill areas.
indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 95% of failed distribution transformers must be replaced within the specified time limit.

indicators.meaning: Resolving specific consumer service connection faults (fuses, service line drops).

indicators.benchmark_meaning: At least 75% of cases must be resolved within the standard; 20% of the remaining cases must be resolved within 24 hours of the complaint.

indicators.meaning: Resolving specific consumer service connection faults (fuses, service line drops).
